topic: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and the Power Iteration

entry_point.discipline_context: Use modal reasoning and matrix-vector calculations familiar from mechanical vibration to motivate an eigenvector as a direction preserved by a matrix.
entry_point.rationale: The learner knows matrices and NumPy but needs a scaffold from eigenpair definitions through one iteration, convergence assumptions, diagnostics, and implementation.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: Modal language provides intuition for a mathematical direction; it does not add physical claims beyond the stated matrix computation.

conditional_item_decisions.rationale: The requested conceptual scope explicitly includes the characteristic equation before iterative computation.
The requested scope explicitly asks for the non-symmetric limitation.
Implementation-level Python and NumPy material are explicitly required.
The requested implementation must preserve positive-integer max_iterations validation and stated return semantics.
The requested scope explicitly includes the worked matrix result.

chapter_sequence.title: Eigenpairs and the characteristic equation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Define eigenvalues and eigenvectors, explain the non-zero vector condition, and connect exact eigenvalue equations with the characteristic equation.

chapter_sequence.title: Symmetry, modal directions, and dominance
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build the real symmetric eigenbasis, define dominant magnitude, and distinguish the power-iteration target from the largest algebraic eigenvalue.

chapter_sequence.title: Deriving one power-iteration step
chapter_sequence.purpose: Derive multiplication and normalization from the eigenbasis expansion, then connect the recurrence to a NumPy implementation.

chapter_sequence.title: Convergence, estimates, and diagnostics
chapter_sequence.purpose: State the convergence assumptions and asymptotic rate, introduce the Rayleigh quotient and residual, and explain failure and scope limitations.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Consolidate theorem scope, perform one structured power-iteration calculation, and diagnose implementation semantics.

implementation_strategy: Use floating NumPy arrays, explicit shape and max_iterations checks, matrix-vector multiplication, normalization before residual evaluation, and a four-value return tuple.
assessment_strategy: Use exactly three final worked exercises: one concept check, one power-iteration hand calculation with a unified structured checker and consistency check, and one executable code diagnostic.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Identify the assumptions needed for convergence and distinguish magnitude dominance, sign ambiguity, and repeated dominance.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Interpret a modal-direction computation without confusing a negative eigenvalue or a non-symmetric matrix with the symmetric convergence case.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Carry out one multiplication-normalization step and compute the Rayleigh quotient and residual from the same chain.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Perform one modal iteration for a small symmetric matrix used as a compact engineering computation.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Diagnose missing validation and premature normalization, then connect corrected code to the stated algorithm and return structure.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Inspect a short eigensolver used in a matrix-based vibration calculation and identify checks that protect iteration semantics.
